summary: Friedrich Knauer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tartu, Jena, and Tübingen under scholars including Meyer, Schroeder, Delbrück, Cappeller, and Roth. He served as a docent at Tartu (1884) and Professor of Comparative Philology at Kyiv (1886–1914).
Friedrich Kurschat worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Königsberg from circa 1836 to 1840 and held a post there from circa 1840 to 1883.

Friedrich Leberecht Wilhelm Schwartz was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He completed his studies at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1840–1842) and the University of Leipzig (circa 1842–1844).

Friedrich Leo worked in linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Bonn, the latter under Hermann Usener. He held posts at Bonn (1877–1881), Kiel (1881–1883), Rostock (1883–1888), Strasbourg (1888–1889), and Göttingen (1889–1914).
Friedrich Lorentz was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (circa 1890–1894), where he studied under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien.

Friedrich Majer worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied law at the University of Jena in 1791, studied under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1799–1803), and later served as a Privatdozent at the University of Jena.

Friedrich Max Müller worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under Brockhaus, Bopp, Schelling, and Burnouf, later holding posts at Oxford from 1850 and as Professor from 1854 to 1900.

Friedrich Müller worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna (under Anton Boller), Göttingen, and Tübingen. He held posts at the Vienna University Library, Austrian National Library, and as Professor at Vienna (1869).

Friedrich Nietzsche worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at Bonn and Leipzig under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, earning his doctorate, and served as a faculty member at the University of Basel from 1869 to 1878.

Friedrich Otto Schrader worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Berlin, Leipzig, Strasbourg, Göttingen (under Franz Kielhorn), and Kiel (under Ernst Leumann). He directed the Adyar Library (1905–1916) and was later a professor at Kiel University.
Friedrich Ottomar Eduard Wilhelm held academic posts at the University of Munich from circa 1910 to 1921 and at the University of Freiburg from circa 1921 to 1928.
Friedrich Ratzel studied at Heidelberg University around 1868. He held posts at the Technical University of Munich (circa 1875–1886) and the University of Leipzig (circa 1886–1904).

Friedrich Rosen worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying under Franz Bopp and Henry Thomas Colebrooke. He taught Hindustani at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1887–1890) and was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London.

Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, Jena, and under Franz Bopp and Hammer-Purgstall. He held professorships at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826–1841) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1841–1849).

Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Heyne, Leipzig, and under Alexander Hamilton and Chézy. He held posts at Jena (1800), Cologne (1804), and TU Dresden (1828).

Friedrich Schleiermacher worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1790), where he held a post from ~1804 to 1807, later holding a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1834).

Friedrich Schrader worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Halle under Richard Pischel, earning his Ph.D. circa 1885–1889, and served as librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft from 1889 to 1891.

Friedrich Stamm worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Münster by 1919 and held positions at the University and State Library of Münster and the Göttingen State and University Library (1921).

Friedrich Stolz was a linguist who studied at Innsbruck under Bernhard Jülg, Leipzig under Georg Curtius, and Graz. At Innsbruck, he served as Privatdozent (1879) and later as Professor of Comparative Linguistics (1886–1912).
Friedrich Streiter was an Indologist who studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin from 1856 to 1861, earning a Ph.D. and studying under Albrecht Weber in 1856.
